- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.10) over recent days, model tends to underpredict; adjust forecast upward by 1–3% for next period.  
- When sentiment is negative (≤-0.20), model often overpredicts; reduce forecast by 1–4% to align with mean reversion bias.  
- Model frequently overshoots after sharp price spikes (e.g., >65.00) — cap forecast at +5% above peak for 3–5 days post-spike.  
- In low-sentiment periods (sentiment <0.05), model shows persistent underprediction; apply +2% bias to early forecast days.  
- Model tends to lag in long-term (30d) forecasts — if sentiment is trending upward, add 1–2% to forecast for next 5–7 days to capture momentum.  
- When sentiment swings sharply (e.g., from +0.17 to -0.28), model often misreads direction — use sentiment reversal as trigger to reset forecast to 1–2% below prior peak.
